pattern_named: 7 of 9 (all `ledger_direction` reversals, #1-7): the SAME notehead's ink is boxed twice by the detector as `ledgerLine` -- once at/near its centre (correctly read as the note's OWN line and excluded by `OWN_LINE_MAX_SPACES`), once at its far rim (top if the note sits above its staff, bottom if below), which lands just past that exclusion radius and gets counted `toward` the OTHER, farther staff. This is not the 2.6c.2 'chord-mate's own line' shape (there is no chord-mate here, no second note) -- it is a single note's own notehead being read as if it contained TWO rungs. Every one of the 7 shows the identical signature: the near staff's `reach_spaces` is 0.01-0.09 (i.e. the note is essentially ON its true staff's first ledger), and the far staff's one credited rung sits within about one notehead-height of that same position.

2 of 9 (`range_veto` reversals, #8-9): ledger_direction is NOT at fault -- it correctly abstains from pointing (the far staff has zero rungs, `reach=false`). The flip comes from the additive `range_veto` term overriding a near-staff placement that both the geometry (note ~1 sp beyond the near staff's edge) and the surrounding print (tied to/from same-staff neighbours) support, in favour of a staff with no nearby ink at all.
next_fix_hypothesis_not_a_decision: For the 7: `ladder_side` should not count a rung whose y falls between the head's own bbox top and bottom (or within roughly one notehead-height of the already-excluded own-line rung) as a step `toward` a candidate -- that band is the note's own ink, not a second ledger, regardless of which side of OWN_LINE_MAX_SPACES it lands on. For the 8/9 pair: `_range_veto` vetoing the staff the ledger geometry (and the surrounding print) both support needs a look at whatever written-range table produced the veto on this instrument at this pitch -- CLAUDE.md rule 7's control (a control must be able to fail) suggests checking whether this veto has EVER been right on a note this close to its own staff, not just whether it fires.
